svg.aria-label: Azure point-to-site VPN: the three protocols and their costs, the authentication by tunnel type matrix and its silent trap, the chain one identity requirement sets off, the routing asymmetry between Windows and non-Windows clients, and the client package as a perishable artefact
svg.title: Azure point-to-site VPN: Entra ID works only with OpenVPN, selecting it with IKEv2 is accepted and does nothing, and Windows clients do not receive BGP-learned routes that non-Windows clients do
svg.text: Three dropdowns, one decision — and a routing table that depends on the client’s OS
THREE PROTOCOLS, AND WHAT EACH COSTS
OpenVPN
SSL/TLS. Penetrates firewalls (TCP 443 outbound). Android, iOS 11+, Windows,
Linux, macOS 13+. TLS 1.2 and 1.3. IPv6 yes. 250 → 10,000 connections.
SSTP
Proprietary TLS. WINDOWS ONLY. No IPv6. Capped at 128 on EVERY SKU.
IKEv2
Standards-based IPsec. Used to connect from macOS 13+. IPv6 yes.
Not supported on the Basic SKU.
AUTHENTICATION BY TUNNEL TYPE — A LATTICE, NOT A MENU
OpenVPN
any subset of Microsoft Entra ID, RADIUS, Azure Certificate
SSTP / IKEv2
RADIUS or Azure Certificate — no Entra ID
Entra ID appears in only the two rows that include OpenVPN. That is the whole constraint.
THE SILENT TRAP: select “IKEv2 and OpenVPN” with Entra ID and Azure ACCEPTS it. Entra ID is used
only on OpenVPN. IKEv2 clients authenticate by the OTHER method and connect fine. No error.
A client needs at least ONE supported pairing to connect. Azure does not care which.
THE CHAIN ONE REQUIREMENT SETS OFF
Conditional Access + MFA
Entra ID
OpenVPN
Azure VPN Client
Windows 11 + macOS
One checkbox at the top, and Linux, iOS, Android and Windows 10 are gone from the bottom.
Certificate
IKEv2, SSTP, OpenVPN · Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS — the WIDEST device reach
RADIUS
works with every tunnel type, and integrates with external identity systems
including multi-factor — the only road to MFA that keeps IKEv2 or SSTP.
WINDOWS AND NON-WINDOWS CLIENTS GET DIFFERENT ROUTES
One VNet 10.1.0.0/16 + on-prem Site1 10.101.0.0/16 over S2S, BGP running. Client pool 192.168.0.0/24.
Windows
gets 10.1.0.0/16 + pool only.
Site1 routes must be added MANUALLY.
non-Windows
Automatic.
Same gateway, same BGP session, same moment. The Windows client does not consume BGP-learned
routes. “It works on my Mac” is a finding about route distribution, not a complaint.
A route in the client table is NOT reachability. Multi-VNet S2S without BGP: non-Windows clients
receive four prefixes and can reach VNet1 only. To reach more, BGP must be used.
Peering reaches ONE hop: directly peered VNets only, not transitive — and that example depends on
Allow gateway transit on the hub and Use remote gateways on the spokes. Both off by default.
THE CLIENT PACKAGE IS PERISHABLE — IN TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS
1. Topology changes
any change to peering or topology — Windows clients must download
and reinstall the package for it to apply.
2. Root cert rotation
Azure rotates gateway root certificates on ITS schedule. This affects
ALL P2S connections — not just certificate-authenticated ones.
The gateway stays healthy. The clients stop connecting.
So the profile needs an owner and a distribution mechanism, not a link in a wiki.
Routing guidance above applies to IKEv2 and OpenVPN only — SSTP’s behaviour is not documented there.
Dates: Azure VPN Client for Linux (Preview) retired 31 Aug 2026, so Entra ID on Linux is closed off — certificate auth on Linux still works via ordinary clients.
Manually registered Azure VPN Clients retire 31 Mar 2028 (Public) and 31 Mar 2029 (Government, 21Vianet). One gateway holds ONE Audience value, so that is a cutover.
Basic SKU is SSTP-only in practice: no IKEv2, no RADIUS, no IPv6, Windows only, 128 users. The default IPsec policy list still accepts AES256 with SHA1 and no PFS.
